seal.statement: Make rs-raft the only partition consensus path. Today a production partition reaches the legacy backend by omission (RAFT_BACKEND_DEFAULT is liferaft and raftBackend is read only from PartitionService construction options that no production caller sets), and the partition write path is liferaft-shaped: applyWrite appends the entry to the legacy durable log through PartitionRaftStorage before proposing, so with rs-raft as the default the seed's first write during cache hydration dies (NOT NULL _raft_log.term) and 37 corpus files fail (census 2026-09-23). After this quest: normal PartitionService construction always yields the frozen rs-raft operation port with no selector, no default fallback and no raftProvider injection as an alternate semantic backend; a write is one propose() through the port whose committed-entry application applies it, with the rs-raft durable store as the only durable log (the legacy log adapter is never written on the partition write path, and the single-replica direct-execution bypass is gone because a solo rs-raft leader commits its own proposals); an explicit legacy backend name is a typed refusal; a partition database holding meaningful legacy consensus state and no rs-raft record fails closed with a typed outcome instead of being reused; and a restarted partition serves its writes from the rs-raft store. Proven by a seed node that bootstraps and serves CREATE TABLE, INSERT and SELECT through production construction with no backend selection at all.

text: Scope widened (R16, supersedes design Q1): the F6 session-transaction isolation LAYER 1 lands inside this quest - the rs-raft durable store refuses to open its transaction or write the commit index while the partition connection is in a user transaction (typed code), the runtime owner checks that admission BEFORE take_ready and returns a non-fatal retryable host outcome for everything but read-status, the transaction owner runs the SQLite COMMIT/ROLLBACK before proposing its marker and proposes no marker while staging, and the write path maps the refusal to a deferred retry. Reason: with the rs-raft store on the partition connection, BEGIN/INSERT/ROLLBACK/INSERT/restart corrupts the durable log (savepoint erased by the session ROLLBACK, MemStorage panics on a non-contiguous log) and falsifies this quest's own receipt restart-serves-writes-from-the-rs-raft-store; a separate quest landed first would be proven on a tree where rs-raft is not the default. LAYER 2 (replicated interactive transactions: operations carried on the TRANSACTION_COMMIT entry and executed on every replica) is its own quest after this one and before certification. Design: solve/quests/raft-rs-single-path-partition-cutover/design-f6-session-transaction-isolation.md

Attempts A1-A3 merged at d86589491: the port decodes committed proposals through the JSON codec and hands the application one frozen {command, index, term, effects}; applyWrite is one propose() through the port with modes {RAFT, REJECTED} (DIRECT branch, legacy append and executePartitionWriteStatement deleted); the committed-entry application builds the commit witness, resolves the pending write in afterCommit, fails closed on UNRECOGNISED types and records STATEMENT_FAILED as an applied outcome; readStatus() is synchronous (the runtime owner's enqueue never cleared its tail once a group went asynchronous, and now keeps a frozen observation per group); PartitionService constructs the rs-raft port by a fixed factory, refuses raftBackend/raftProvider options with a typed code; raft-backend-selection and its constants are deleted; the legacy-state detector refuses meaningful legacy consensus rows without an rs-raft record; SQLiteLogAdapter/PartitionRaftStorage are no longer constructed on the partition path; HLC warm-up, mirror replay and prepared-state reconstruction read the rs-raft store through DDL-free static readers bounded by the applied index; the dead partition-replication-handler direct-apply path is deleted. Six sealed receipts green locally (6/6); rs-raft backend suite green; whole corpus running on the lab node.

Scope widened (R16), recorded after the fact on the verifier's B1: attempt A5 (44b09a430) fixed F11 (inbound drained on delivery), F15 (a per-peer delivery failure is never a group or runtime fatal), F16 (ADD_PEER proposed with the canonical replicaIdentity shape by one admission owner, leader only), F17 (unreserved peer identities are a typed status, readStatus never throws) and F18 (an honest progress probe) inside this quest. Reason: the corpus with rs-raft as the only path proved multi-replica partitions unusable without them (dt6 live-voter witnesses; group-A residue), and the sealed statement's claim that rs-raft is the only partition consensus path is false while a joiner cannot catch up and one unreachable follower unseats the leader. The runtime blast-radius gap (epic) remains open beyond F15: F9 (reconstruction leaves the lone leader leaderless) and the shared-runtime replacement on application host failures are recorded, not fixed here.

Round 1 REJECT: B1 unrecorded widening (now recorded), B2 duplicate-key INSERT under a new entryId acknowledged success:true/changes:0 (replay suppression keyed on the constraint, not the entry identity), B3 impact contract partition-raft-operation-port still names both providers and the transaction-owner/store-admission interaction has no contract; twelve findings F-a..F-l recorded in verification-round-1.md

Attempts A4-A8 merged at 97c4dc8e7: F6 layer 1 (store persistence admission, runtime admission before take_ready, markers proposed after the SQLite COMMIT/ROLLBACK, no PREPARE marker while staging, deferred retry, a held Ready keeps the process alive; W1-W7 green); the dt6 learner-promotion witnesses re-homed on live rs-raft voters; A5 runtime prerequisites for multi-replica partitions (inbound drained on delivery, per-peer delivery failures, one admission owner with the canonical ADD_PEER shape, unreserved peer identities typed, an honest progress probe); A6 fixture migrations and explicit-unavailability witnesses; A7 corrective after verification round 1 (statement-failure determinism boundary, campaign refusal fails init, honest admission outcomes, impact contracts repaired); A8 durable committed-statement outcome record so retries are deterministic on every replica and after restart; complexity baseline tightened 1816 -> 1814.

Round 2 REJECT: B4 dt-movielens-raft-peer-cohort-pruning-election red on the head (the rewritten witness expects bootstrap voters in the double's status; the admission owner proposes only on a leader); B1-B3 resolved with fresh evidence incl. real SQLITE_FULL injection; findings F-m..F-v recorded in verification-round-2.md

Scope widened (R16) for F-m: an environmental SQLite failure on a lone leader now wedges the partition until process restart (the runtime is replaced and the sole voter never campaigns again while isLeader stays true), where the deleted direct-execution path returned the failure and continued. That is F9 made reachable on every seed system partition by this quest, so its narrow form lands here: after runtime reconstruction a group that was the sole voter and leader campaigns again and the partition's leadership observation re-syncs from the port; a witness injects SQLITE_FULL on a lone leader and requires the next write to succeed without a process restart. The broader blast-radius design (a follower's persistence failure replacing the shared runtime for the leader in the same process, F-n) stays recorded for its own quest.
